title: Binary wire protocol design
subtitle: I design binary wire protocols when the problem needs them: the Teams audio link with byte-identical C# and Rust implementations, the broker's token-level transport, the vector store's RPC wire.

stats.label: integers describe any GPU consumer to the broker
RPC variants on the vector store's CBOR wire
frame limit on that wire, with a streaming fetch for larger windows

lede: I choose the wire per link from what the traffic costs and who has to debug it, and I prove cross-language implementations equal with golden vectors. Helix had to connect Microsoft's real-time media stack, which runs only on Windows, to my voice engine on Linux, without putting call audio in a third party's hands. I decided on a purpose-built binary link over one authenticated full-duplex WebSocket per call, implemented twice, in C# in the .NET media service and in Rust in the voice engine's endpoint. When the link drops, the bridge reconnects inside the same Teams call. The bridge is told in A self-hosted colleague in a Teams call.
quote: Binary goes where the traffic is real-time audio, billions of tokens or bulk tensors; where payloads are small, a readable wire wins on diagnosability.
evidence: Binary protocol design: one audio and video link for Teams calls implemented in C# and Rust and proved byte-identical against golden vectors before either carries a call.
Message broker and queue design: a token-level transport where any GPU consumer is described by 4 integers and one connection carries its batches, completions and heartbeats.
RPC and serialisation design: a vector store wire of 33 length-prefixed CBOR RPC variants with a 16 MiB frame limit and a streaming fetch, and a readable JSON socket where payloads are small.
author: Corey James
